Token embeddings substitute for contextual pre-LayerNorm inputs; positions, upstream states, MLP, residual and later-layer effects are omitted.

report.analysis_inputs: Frozen candidate JSONL and their metadata only; no corpus or model evaluation.
report.graph_definition: Triple (b,a,c) is directed edge (b,a)->(a,c). A path of at least 4 tokens requires at least one target pair equal to a source pair.
report.marginal_necessary_conditions: For edge (b,a,c) to extend, a must appear in the previous-token set and c in the current-token set. These conditions are necessary, not sufficient.
report.source_outdegree_definition: Number of emitted destination edges for each selected (previous,current) pair.
implications: Every run has 0 exact overlapping triple edges, before path repetition restrictions are applied.
Final selection has disjoint previous/current token sets, which alone makes all >=4-token overlap paths impossible.
Zero generated paths therefore reflects the disconnected norm-selected graph; it does not prove absence of sequence information in the model.
Triple semantic success/failure must be measured separately by the independent corpus verifier.
A future closed-vocabulary or normalized-basis graph is a new exploratory protocol, not a retroactive success under this fixed protocol.
